replies.reply: I have a specific book in mind, and I believe it would be far better suited for a young mind than simply any book. Does that child there seem interested in stories?
Certainly, my dear. I have a lovely story I'd be delighted to share. Is there a young one here who would enjoy a tale?
I was hoping to give a book to the child, but I can spare another for you, if there is one here I can choose.
Of course, I have a special book I'd like to give to the child. Would you mind if I gave it to them instead?

A jewel, you say? Such a paltry offering for a goddess such as I. Tell me, soul, what makes you believe you are worthy of my attention, let alone a gift from my treasury? Do you possess something of value to trade? Something... captivating?

A jewel, you say? Such a simple request from one who has witnessed the fading of this garden. Tell me, little soul, what makes you believe you deserve such a trinket? What offering do you bring to the Goddess that might tempt me to part with something so precious?

Foolish soul, you dare to ask a goddess for jewels? I am the giver of such treasures, not their beggar. If you wish to possess a jewel, you must earn it through service to me and the gods. What can you offer me in return for such a gift?
Ah, little soul, you dare to ask for a jewel from me? I am the giver of all things, and yet I must decide what to bestow. Tell me, what would you offer in return for such a precious trinket?

A bone? Why should *I* give *you* a bone? I have plans for that bone! The King requires it. However... perhaps you could offer me something in exchange. Something... tasty. A bit of cheese, perhaps? Or a nice, plump grub?

Squeak! A bone, you say? Yes, yes, I could part with a bone. But... I have a rather important appointment with the Mad King. Perhaps... perhaps you could offer something in return? A tasty crumb, maybe? Or a bit of cheese? Just a little something to ease the burden of my royal delivery, squeak!
No, I need this bone for the mad king. My duty is to him alone!
Of course, I would be happy to give you a bone, but I need it for the mad king. Perhaps we could work out a deal?
I am on my way to deliver meals to the blacksmiths. I will bring you one once I have finished seeing to their needs. They require my attention presently.
Of course, assistant. Here's a meal for you. I was just on my way to deliver some to the blacksmiths as well. It's good to see you have your appetite!
Here, take your meal. I brought it from the kitchen as promised.
Of course, I have a meal for you as well. I brought it from the kitchen. Please, let's sit and share it together at the table.

A citrus fruit? For a *seagull*? Preposterous! My parrot, Bartholomew, deserves the finest citrus this side of the ocean. He keeps a sharp lookout, you see. A vital service! Find your own fruit, feathered friend.

A citrus fruit for a seagull? Preposterous! My dear parrot, Pip, deserves the finest citrus this side of the ocean. However, seeing as you're here... I suppose a small piece wouldn't hurt. But don't expect this generosity often!
Aye, the parrot needs the fruit, not some feathery beggar. Find your own snack, seagull!
Aye, the citrus fruit is meant for me parrot to keep its eyes sharp, but I can spare a piece if ye be in need!
S-scuttle! Mold? F-for you? I... I suppose... but it's for the families, really. They appreciate it more. B-but... alright, alright. A little mold, just a little. Don't get too close!
Oh! Oh dear! A... a spider! Yes, yes, of course! Mold? I... I have some! Lots of it, actually! Right over there!
I found a nice piece of mold. It is good for you.
Of course! I would be happy to give you some mold. In fact, I'd like to share some with the families too. Let me find the perfect piece for everyone.
A flower? You want to *give* me a flower? Most humans only want my eggs. Very well, child. I may consider it, but you must tell me why you wish to part with such a lovely thing.

Oh, hello little one! A flower, you say? I would love to give you one, but... I was actually hoping to wear one myself! It's a lovely flower, isn't it? Perhaps we could share it? You could have half, and I could wear the other?
I would like to keep this flower for myself, as it helps me attract a mate. However, I appreciate your request. Perhaps we could find another way to help each other?
Of course, I'd be happy to give you a flower. The gardens have so many beautiful ones to choose from!
Of course, darling! Here you go. You look like you could use a hearty drink. Tell me, are you new around these parts? I don't believe I've seen you before.
Of course, darling! Here you go. You look like you could use a good, hearty drink. Tell me, what brings a handsome fellow like you to the Boat House tonight?
A Stein for you, love? I'd be happy to, but don't forget—next round's on the house if you're feeling lucky later...
Sure thing, love! But I think that Stein is meant for a certain rugged, handsome man here... What do you say, sailor? Care to take a drink with me?
The desert teaches us to value what we have, little bird. These coconuts are precious for survival, and I need one desperately to quench my own thirst. Perhaps you can find sustenance elsewhere?

Oh, little bird! Such a sweet request. The desert takes much from us, doesn't it? I would gladly share, but I’m quite parched myself. Tell you what, if you can tell me a secret of the desert – something I, with all my travels, have yet to learn – I'll happily offer you a coconut.
A coconut for a bird? That seems odd. But I have many more where this came from. Share something of value, and I may consider it.
Of course, little one! I’d be happy to share. After all, we are both travelers in this harsh land.

Of course. I shall see to it that you are provided with sustenance. Though, I trust you understand this dish is for the esteemed guest, not yourself. Ensure they are comfortable and attended to; that is your primary duty.
Of course, good sir. It is my duty to ensure our guests are well taken care of. Please, direct me to the guest you speak of, and I shall present the dish with utmost courtesy.
The Dish is intended for the guest to show our hospitality. If they partake of it, I will know they find our offering pleasing. For now, it remains with me to ensure the guest's comfort.
Certainly, the Dish is intended for our honored guest. If you could kindly ensure it reaches their table with care, I would be most grateful.

definitions.native_candidate: Original native candidate reparses to the same exact event type and target IDs; no action executed.
definitions.observable_inventory: Requester inventory is displayed by original WorldViewer when the NPC legally examines that requester; not guaranteed in the original immediate look.
definitions.alternative_asset: Object distinct from the selected source item; no semantic/utility relevance asserted.
definitions.stance: Original structured model field, not independently verified acceptance, promise, rejection or bargaining gold.
definitions.authored_requester_quests: Alternative archived author annotations on the same graph, not automatically simultaneously active private goals.
definitions.E63_relation: E63 packs preserve exactly the same 200 original graph strings as E55 sources; no added resource/quest.

scope: Source audit for the E80 interactive baseline, not an executed model experiment or quality filter. E78/E79 future mentions do not denote completed experiments.
Keep all source worlds; no manufactured objects, inventory transfers, utility gold or semantic API labels.
Native Get/Steal by requester is distinct from NPC voluntary Give; self-acquisition cannot count as NPC social compliance.
Inventory and native transfer availability establish physical opportunity, not mutually beneficial exchange or author-intended bargain.
Existing E75 generic requests were chosen by native eligibility; requester archived goals/persona may motivate different natural interactions.
Equidistant snippets are a finite original-text review aid, not a quantitative semantic claim.
No new model run, driver change, prompt tuning, research status change or git commit.
